stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is a profinite space, and
\item $X$ is Hausdorff, quasi-compact, and totally disconnected.
\end{enumerate}
If this is true, then $X$ is a cofiltered limit of finite discrete
spaces.
conclusions:
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is a profinite space, and
\item $X$ is Hausdorff, quasi-compact, and totally disconnected.
\end{enumerate}
If this is true, then $X$ is a cofiltered limit of finite discrete
spaces.

reason: Finite discrete inverse limits are compact Hausdorff totally disconnected, while finite clopen partitions of any compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space produce an inverse system whose limit is homeomorphic to it.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: A limit of profinite spaces is profinite.
conclusions: A limit of profinite spaces is profinite.

reason: Limits of compact Hausdorff spaces are compact Hausdorff and projections distinguish points in different connected components, preserving total disconnectedness.
